title: FrameGraph and custom render passes
summary: Declare render resources and pass dependencies, then understand graph compilation and resource lifetimes.

blocks.text: FrameGraph collects Pass objects and virtual texture/buffer handles. Pass.setup uses GraphBuilder to declare resources; Pass.execute receives RenderContext with resolved physical resources and encoder state. Decorators read/write/create register handle fields, while the underlying arrays retain dependency metadata.

Compilation builds dependencies, topologically sorts passes and rejects cycles. Passes not contributing to an unculled sink can be culled. ResourcePool can reuse compatible transient resources with non-overlapping lifetimes. Persistent imports keep external resources across frames and must be refreshed when the underlying texture changes.

The current FrameGraph.addPass receives a Pass instance. It does not take a name and callback builder. Build a Pass subclass or reuse an existing PostProcessPass, declare its input/output handles and connect its output to the pipeline’s RenderIO. A pass that only writes an unconsumed texture may be culled.

Custom compute work can use CustomComputePass or the scene compute queue. Custom raster work can use CustomRenderPass and RenderPass-compatible contracts. Declare dependencies for every texture and buffer actually used; WebGPU cannot infer the intended application dataflow from an arbitrary shader string.

Pass setup and graph compilation describe the frame structure. Execute encodes one frame. Allocate stable pipelines/resources outside execute when possible, update uniforms for frame time inside the intended update path and invalidate the graph when topology or descriptor changes require a rebuild. Do not keep a transient texture view after its graph lifetime.
Two small passes expose one explicit producer-to-consumer resource dependency.
